Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

predictmeans 2.0.0

predictmeans 2.0.0 is a major release. Defaults changed where simulations or the literature showed a more reliable method; each such change names the argument that gives the 1.x result. Results are checked in the tests against SAS PROC MIXED and Genstat runs, pbkrtest, nlme and emmeans. Every removed argument or function stops with its 2.0 spelling, the value given filled in; nothing is silently ignored. vignette("migrating") shows 1.1.1 and 2.0 code side by side.

Breaking changes

Removed functions

Removed Use instead
smZ(), smoothZ = smooths in the formula of semireg() / semireg_tmb(), e.g. s(x, bs = "os")
permglmer(), permglmmTMB() permlmer() (they were the same function)
permanova.lmer() permmodels(model, type = ) (Freedman-Lane; other p-values)
R2_glmm() R2_model(model) (same values, as numbers)
ci_mcp() predictmeans(..., letter_ci = TRUE)

Renamed arguments

  • Dotted names are snake_case: conf.level -> conf_level, letterCI -> letter_ci, as.is -> as_is, test.statistic -> test_statistic, max.degree -> max_degree, drop.unused.levels -> drop_unused_levels. Result columns keep the broom names (conf.low, std.error, p.value).
  • level (a significance level) -> conf_level = 1 - level in predictmeans(), contrastmeans(), covariatemeans(), pm_slopes(), semipred(), permstats(), PMplot(). In varcomp() level was a confidence level already: conf_level with the same value.
  • Df -> df_method = <number>; df_term(type = ) -> df_term(df_method = ).
  • covariateV -> at in covariatemeans(), semipred(), Kmatrix().
  • semipred(semireg = ) -> semipred(model = ); simultaneous = TRUE -> band = "simultaneous".
  • permlmer(lmer0, lmer1) -> permlmer(model0, model1).
  • residplot(level = ) -> re_level; CookD(idn = ) -> id.
  • semireg(ngbinomial = TRUE) -> semireg_tmb(family = glmmTMB::nbinom2).

Removed arguments

  • Back-transformation: transOff (put the offset inside trans, e.g. trans = function(x) exp(x) - 1); count (Poisson and negative binomial means are detected); responsen (read from the model).
  • Printing: prtnum, ndecimal, prt. Nothing is printed during a call; use print(x) or print(x, digits = ).
  • predictmeans() plot arguments: plot, plot_args, which.plots, mplot, barplot, pplot, bkplot, prtplt, plotord, lineplot, lsd_bar, jitterv, plottitle, plotxlab, plotylab, basesz. plot = FALSE is still accepted.
  • covariatemeans() (trellis, plotord, mtitle, ci, point, jitterv) and semipred() (trellis, scales, plotord, ci, point, jitterv, threeD): use autoplot() on the result; plot_args = list(...) still works (superseded).
  • newwd (predictmeans(), covariatemeans(), residplot(), CookD(), PMplot()), residplot(ask), PMplot(margin, legendx): ggplot2 draws in the current device.
  • semireg(): ncenter, nscale, resp_scale (variables are used as they are); predict_info in semireg() and semireg_tmb() (always kept).
  • permmodels(fo = ): the formula is read from the model.

Other changes to scripts

  • predictmeans() draws no plots. Use autoplot(pm) or plot(pm) with type = "means", "bar", "ci" (the 1.x back-transformed plot) or "pvalue". The result has no predictmeansPlot or predictmeansBarPlot.
  • covariatemeans() and semipred() draw only when asked: plot = TRUE, autoplot(), or options(predictmeans.plot = TRUE).
  • pairwise defaults to NULL: comparisons are made when adj, atvar, permlist, letter_ci or pairwise = TRUE asks for them. pairwise only sets what is printed.
  • The “Pairwise LSDs” matrix is no longer printed; each pair’s LSD is in pairs$lsd.
  • covariatemeans()$pltdf is now $pred_df (as in semipred()); $pltdf still works with a message.
  • semipred(threeD) / autoplot(type = "3d") gives one plotly widget, not a list.
  • contrastmeans() returns class "contrastmeans" with adj.conf.low/adj.conf.high columns; pm_slopes() column slope is now estimate.
  • se_ranef() returns a data frame (class pm_ranef); as.list() gives the 1.x list of SE matrices.
  • summary() of a semireg() / semireg_tmb() fit returns a list with the mixed-model summary in $model.
  • Results keep the data needed for plots, not the fitted model.
  • fit$knots_lst, range_lst, type_lst and smoothZ_call are gone; refit models saved with smZ().
  • library(predictmeans) attaches lme4 and nlme only. glmmTMB moved to Imports and lmerTest to Suggests: call library(glmmTMB) or library(lmerTest) when needed.
  • car, pbkrtest, HRW, lmeInfo, lmeSplines, plotly and splines2 moved to Suggests; plyr is no longer used. mgcv moved to Imports.
  • ncore defaults to 1 (was 3) in predictmeans(), permlmer() and permmodels().
  • residplot(id) defaults to 3: the three largest residuals are labelled.

Changes that affect results

  • anova(<lmer fit>, type = "I") now uses Kenward-Roger df and F, like Types II and III, and ddf = "Satterthwaite" gives the previous table; both equal SAS PROC MIXED HTYPE=1. Type III tests a nested term (A + A:B) within each level of the outer factor, as SAS (it had 0 df), and the “empty cells” note no longer appears for nested factors or for factors that only have main effects.
  • REML lmer fits use Kenward-Roger adjusted standard errors in predictmeans(), contrastmeans() and covariatemeans(), as SAS DDFM=KR and emmeans. Unbalanced designs change slightly. 1.x: vcov_adjust = FALSE.
  • Kenward-Roger uses the observed information of the variance parameters, as SAS; it stays valid with missing values. pbkrtest’s version: df_method = "KR-expected".
  • Degrees of freedom are chosen by model class (df_method = "auto"): Kenward-Roger for REML lmer, lme and gls; Satterthwaite for ML fits; inner-outer df for GLMMs; z tests for Poisson, binomial and negative binomial glm. Simulations showed the old df rejected too often (or too rarely for glm). 1.x: df_method = "residual" (or "containment" for lme/gls).
  • permmodels() uses Freedman-Lane permutations (method = "auto"), so other terms keep their effects. 1.x: method = "raw".
  • Permutation tests of mixed models decorrelate residuals with the symmetric square root of their covariance; the 1.x Cholesky factor depended on the order of the data. Raw p-values for mixed models also differ.
  • Permutation p-values are (b + 1)/(B + 1) unless perms holds a complete enumeration.
  • permlmer() with different fixed effects refits both models by ML, so the permuted statistic is the printed likelihood ratio.
  • se_ranef() defaults to the prediction error SE (type = "prediction", SAS “Std Err Pred”), larger than 1.x. 1.x: type = "conditional".
  • Type III tests do not depend on the model’s contrasts (sum-to-zero hypotheses, as SAS Type 3).
  • Means over empty cells keep the 1.x average of the observed cells, but their pairs are compared on the cells both means have; the 1.x comparison rejected too often in simulations.
  • Means that depend on aliased coefficients are NA, with a message; estimable differences are shown.
  • aov() with Error() is analysed by strata, as Genstat, with missing values estimated as Genstat’s ANOVA. It was refitted as lmer. 1.x: fit the mixed model yourself.
  • A response transformed in the formula (log(y), log(y + c), sqrt(y), …) is back-transformed by default. trans = I keeps the model scale. A given trans is now used also for models with a link.
  • bias_adjust = TRUE gives the mean exactly by quadrature. The 1.x-style second-order formula: bias_adjust = "taylor".
  • covariatemeans() with a log link or trans = exp draws the back-transformed fitted value; 1.x added half the SE.
  • The printed LSD goes with the adjusted p-values (Tukey HSD, Bonferroni, Sidak, Scheffe, mvt critical values); with atvar it uses the pairs within each level. adj = "none" is unchanged.
  • letter_ci = TRUE reads letters from comparison intervals at the comparisons’ level; drop a 1.x level = 0.166.
  • semipred() limits are two-sided at the stated level (1.x defaults gave 90%). Gaussian semireg() fits get t limits with Satterthwaite df; generalized fits include smoothing-parameter uncertainty (unconditional).
  • semireg() uses the nloptwrap optimizer. 1.x: control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa").
  • Gaussian semireg_tmb() fits are REML, as documented (they were ML).
  • glmer Poisson back-transformed means are counts, as for glm and glmmTMB.

New features

Means and comparisons

  • Stable result tables means, pairs and settings with fixed column names; tidy(), glance(), as.data.frame(), coef() and vcov() methods. The 1.x elements are kept.
  • weights = "equal", "proportional" (SAS OM), "outer", "cells", "flat" for averaging cells.
  • Adjustments "sidak", "scheffe" and "mvt"; adjusted confidence limits adj.conf.low/adj.conf.high.
  • Comparison intervals: two means differ when their intervals do not overlap.
  • contrast_family(), specify_contrast() (contrasts by level name), pm_joint() (joint F tests and slices), pm_slopes() (slopes per level), contrastmeans(joint = TRUE).
  • Equivalence tests (equivalence =); robust covariances (vcov = "HC0" to "HC3", ~ cluster, or a matrix or function).
  • Response-scale means with delta-method SEs, ratios and odds ratios; average = "response"; pm_boxcox() and pm_yeojohnson() for formulas.
  • mean_type = "overall" for zero-inflated glmmTMB models.
  • Kmatrix() handles poly(), splines, transformations, gam smooths, covariates by name and combinations of factors that are not a model term; cov_reduce and exclude.
  • Faster with many means and pairs; more than 100 means without comparisons skip the pair table.

Tests and degrees of freedom

  • anova() of lmer fits: type1_basis = "fitted" builds Type I hypotheses from the fitted model (X’V^-1X), as Genstat, instead of X’X (SAS, lmerTest; the default); ddf = "KR-average" gives Genstat’s d.d.f. with an unadjusted F. Together they reproduce Genstat’s Wald and F statistics; Genstat prints each term’s Type II d.d.f., here each test has the d.d.f. of its own hypothesis.

  • df_method = "Kenward-Roger", "KR-expected", "KR-average" (Genstat), "Satterthwaite", "containment", "between-within", "inner-outer", "residual" or a number, also for lme and gls.

  • anova() of lmer fits with Kenward-Roger or Satterthwaite F tests, Types I, II, III, without lmerTest.

  • Kenward-Roger and Satterthwaite computed without n x n matrices; much faster.

  • Ordinal models: MASS::polr() and ordinal::clm() fits (location effects). Means on the latent scale (as emmeans’ mode = "latent"), pairs as log odds ratios of a higher class, z tests; mean_type = "prob" adds the class probabilities at each mean and mean_type = "mean_class" the expected class, with delta-method SEs. Also ordinal::clmm() fits, for a typical subject (random effects at 0), with the inner-outer df of GLMMs (z tests rejected 11% of true nulls at 5% with 6 clusters). Checked against emmeans. Summaries say “z tests” when the df are infinite. VGAM::vglm() fits of the ordinal families cumulative, propodds, acat, cratio and sratio with parallel = TRUE: the same latent means, oriented so that a positive difference means higher classes, whatever the family and reverse (SEs from VGAM’s expected information). vglm fits of other families (e.g. poissonff), which gave link-scale means with t tests before, now stop with a message. nnet::multinom(), VGAM::vglm() with multinomial() and ordinal vglm fits with non-parallel slopes: the class is a factor of the means, pairs within each class. mean_type = "prob" (default): class probabilities on the logit scale, back-transformed with limits inside 0-1, pairs as log odds ratios (with two classes the same as a binomial glm); "prob_diff": differences of probabilities (as emmeans’ mode = "prob"); "link": the model’s linear predictors; "mean_class" for ordinal families. Probabilities averaged over other factors on the probability scale; delta-method SEs, z tests; advice on separation (a class absent at some levels). Checked against emmeans; other functions stop for these fits. Where the cumulative curves of a non-parallel fit cross (negative probabilities), the means that use those points are NA with a caution.

  • weights = "proportional" (and "outer", "cells", "flat") count cases instead of rows where a row holds several: binomial and quasibinomial responses of any class (trials) and class responses (multinom, polr, clm, clmm, vglm with case weights). Aggregated data and one row per case then weight the factor combinations alike (as emmeans); covariates are still set from the rows. settings$weights_by says which. semireg means stop for weights other than "equal" (they were ignored).

  • New article “Ordinal and categorical responses”: latent means of cumulative link models, class probabilities of multinomial and non-parallel fits, the scales and the checks.

Mixed models and variance components

  • New heritability(): line-mean (entry-mean) heritability from an lmer fit with random genotypes, in the standard form and the mixed-model forms of Cullis et al. (2006), Piepho and Möhring (2007) and Oakey et al. (2006), for unbalanced trials; method = "all" shows them side by side. method = "family" gives the narrow-sense heritability of a single plant from half-sib or full-sib families (relationship), and "repeatability" that of single records; "reliability" (mean reliability) and "simulated" (Piepho and Möhring’s simulated r2). Plot means: within_variance, within_n give the single-plant variance. SEs: delta method, or a parametric bootstrap (nboot). Works with weights, several genotype x environment terms, genotypes nested in a fixed factor (with a note) and boundary fits (genotypic variance 0). Reproduces every value of Schmidt et al. (2019, Figure 1) for the oats alpha design.
  • varcomp() for every model class, with observed-information SEs and Satterthwaite intervals; test = TRUE tests each component (likelihood ratio, boundary mixture or parametric bootstrap).
  • se_ranef() for lmer, glmer, glmmTMB, lme and semireg fits, with any covariance structure; checked against SAS PROC MIXED; predict = TRUE adds the fixed part to each BLUP.
  • R2_model() with method = "piepho" or "nakagawa", for every model class; reproduces Piepho (2023).

Permutation and bootstrap

  • Freedman-Lane permutations for lm, glm, lmer, lme, gls, glmer and glmmTMB, with or without refits (refit).
  • permlmer() tests GLMMs on the working scale; method = "quantile" for 0/1 responses.
  • Permutation confidence limits, permutation Tukey and adj = "westfall"; robust = TRUE (HC3, sign flips).
  • bootmodels() for parametric bootstrap p-values, usable as permlist.
  • permindex() and perms for restricted permutations; permstats(); permcombine().

Semiparametric models

  • Smooths in the formula of semireg() and semireg_tmb(): mgcv bases, by =, s(x, f) and s(x, f1*f2) deviation curves, bs = "os", bs = "ztps", bs = "user", t2() tensor products, random curves (s(x) | g), glmmTMB covariance structures.
  • semipred(): simultaneous bands, deriv = 1, 2, curve differences with a test, bias_adjust, boundary; semiboundary() for two-dimensional data.
  • anova() of semireg() fits with tests of smooth variances; predictmeans() on semireg() fits.
  • Fits print a short account of the smooth terms; coef(), vcov(), fitted() and other methods work.

Plots

  • autoplot() for every result: means, bars, confidence limits, p-value heat maps, curves, surfaces, 3-D, differences; x, group, panel, interval, data, scales.
  • residplot(), CookD() and PMplot() are drawn with ggplot2 for every model class; residplot(interactive = TRUE) uses plotly. Many overlapping points are drawn as transparent open circles (or, with dense = "bins", as shaded bins with the outstanding points on top); the Q-Q plot of many residuals keeps every tail point.

Model checking and advice

  • pm_check(): a table of checks of a fitted model (outliers, influence, normality, equal variances, dispersion, separation, collinearity, …).
  • New residvariogram(): the sample variogram of a model’s residuals over a row x column field layout or coordinates (also latitude/longitude, by direction), one per trial with by, with a global envelope from data simulated from the fitted model and a test of spatial pattern; advice suggests a spatial model when neighbouring plots are more alike than the model allows. The estimator reproduces Genstat’s FVARIOGRAM (Brooms Barn example). pm_check(row = , col = ) adds the check. Rows or columns numbered within blocks stop with a message.
  • Advice printed with results when the fit or data call for it; advice() returns it, options(predictmeans.advice = FALSE) hides it.

Results and extension

  • Exported generics pm_coef(), pm_vcov(), pm_basis(), pm_data(), pm_df(), pm_linkinv() for new model classes (?pm_coef). The columns of the design are matched to the coefficients by name; a name without a column stops with a message, never a silent mismatch.
  • pm_coef() of an aov fit keeps its aliased coefficients as NA, as for lm and glm; every front end now reads a fit’s coefficients and covariance only through pm_coef() and pm_vcov().
  • ?pm_coef says what a new model class gets: means and pairs need coef(), vcov() and terms(); residplot() and pm_check() also fitted() and residuals() (else they stop and say so); the other functions list the classes they handle.
  • New data sets, including Caschool, DataExam5.2, copper and M. P. Wand’s examples.

Bug fixes

  • Estimability checks (means, their pairs, empty-cell contrasts, slopes) no longer depend on the units of a covariate: with a site mean in large units an aliased slope was reported as 0 with SE 0.

  • anova() of lmer fits: a factor nested in another only in the data (y ~ G + T) is tested within it in Type III, as with G/T, with a caution to write G/T; balanced nested designs are no longer called unbalanced; ML fits get Satterthwaite df with a message instead of a Kenward-Roger label; a failed Kenward-Roger adjustment in Types II and III falls back to Satterthwaite.

  • pm_slopes() gives no pairs when the slopes are equal by the model (no covariate x term interaction).

  • covariatemeans() drew curves that the data do not identify (a covariate constant within the levels of a factor in the model, as a site mean with site; or a function of other factors). It now stops with a message pointing to contr = and pm_slopes(), which estimate the differences between curves; single points that cannot be estimated are NA, with advice.

  • pm_slopes() gave a slope of 0 with SE 0 when the covariate is aliased with a factor (a site mean with site in the model). Such slopes are now NA, with advice; their differences are kept. The slopes table has an estimable column, as the means table.

  • autoplot() of means by group with the data (data = TRUE) works with ggplot2 3.4, as DESCRIPTION promises (it stopped: “position_jitterdodge() requires at least one aesthetic to dodge by”).

  • Permutation tests, bootmodels() and variance-component tests of lmer/glmer fits with missing values work with older lme4 (1.1-35 dropped the missing rows twice in refit()).

  • A glmmTMB fit with aliased coefficients (e.g. combinations of levels without data) no longer stops every means function with “logical subscript too long”; the means equal those of the same lmer ML fit.

  • semireg() with a deviation smooth s(x, f1*f2) no longer gives the warning “number of items to replace”.

  • permlmer() reports lme4 convergence warnings of the permuted refits once, as a count, instead of one warning per refit.

  • Tukey p-values within atvar levels used the number of pairs instead of means.

  • predictmeans() failed for lmer models with a missing treatment combination, and for ML lmer fits.

  • predictmeans() with permlist and atvar failed; a user Df for lmer gave NA p-values.

  • Factor levels containing ":" broke the pairwise tables.

  • Within-atvar adjusted p-values could be matched to the wrong pairs.

  • contrastmeans() failed with any missing treatment combination.

  • Kenward-Roger ignored prior weights and offsets of lmer fits.

  • semireg() 0/1 responses had SEs 15-25% too small; Gamma and inverse-Gaussian SEs were too small.

  • semireg() gaussian fits had wrong anova() df and varcomp() SEs.

  • semireg_tmb() negative binomial SEs were scaled by theta; zero-inflated bands were too narrow.

  • semipred(contr = ) bands of generalized models were wrong.

  • varcomp() SEs for glmer and limits for glmmTMB were wrong.

  • R2_glmm() was wrong for some glmmTMB families, offsets and correlated random effects.

  • permindex() with block or group returned indices for sorted data.

  • permmodels() permuted only one column of cbind() responses; type I lmer tables compared different statistics.

  • permmodels() and CookD() could refit with a data set of the same name found elsewhere.

  • CookD() failed for every lmer model.

Documentation

  • The help pages of anova() for lmer and semireg fits and of se_ranef() show their usage (CRAN pre-test: “Rd files without ”).
  • New vignettes: “Migrating from predictmeans 1.x”, “Checking the model”, “Missing cells and non-estimable means”, “Smooth curves in mixed models”, “Permutation and bootstrap tests”, “Link and response scale”, “Contrasts, joint tests and slopes”, and “Matching SAS PROC MIXED” (the SAS and Genstat reference runs).
  • vignette("predictmeans") rewritten, with a table of default df by model class.
  • Help pages written with roxygen2; ?advice lists every advice id.
  • A pkgdown website with worked-example articles: an overview, tree improvement, and adjusted R² for GLMMs reproducing Piepho (2023).

The full development log of 2.0.0 is in the package source, file dev/NEWS-2.0-development.md.
